name: Citizenship by Registration (Marriage)

requirements.blocker_text: Must be the spouse, widow, or widower of a Sri Lankan citizen -- the provision applies regardless of the applicant's sex.
One year's residence in Ceylon/Sri Lanka immediately preceding the application, and full age and sound mind.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 1 year's residence immediately before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: Registration is discretionary: the Minister must approve the application, generally on public interest grounds -- meeting the residence and marital-status criteria does not by itself entitle the applicant to registration.

evidence_required.document: Proof of 1 year's residence in Sri Lanka

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR-hosted legal database) -- Sri Lanka Citizenship Act No. 18 of 1948, Section 12: a spouse, widow, or widower of a citizen may apply for registration, requiring full age and sound mind, one year's residence in Ceylon immediately preceding the application, and Ministerial approval on public interest grounds

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sri Lanka). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 sourcing only (see lk_citizenship_by_descent.json's notes on lawnet.gov.lk's SSL failure). GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: Section 12 is gender-neutral on its face ('spouse, widow, or widower'), unlike the many one-directional gendered marriage-citizenship provisions found elsewhere in this dataset (Qatar, Bahrain, Nigeria, Sudan, Somalia, Pakistan, Ghana). However, it is explicitly DISCRETIONARY -- Ministerial approval on public-interest grounds is a real, sourced precondition, not a rubber stamp, so this is a materially weaker entitlement than an automatic marriage-citizenship provision even though it applies equally regardless of the applicant's sex. This is the closest thing Sri Lanka's Act has to an ordinary path to citizenship for a long-term foreign resident short of the ultra-narrow 25-person/year 'distinguished service' quota (see lk_citizenship_distinguished_service.json) -- there is no general residence-based naturalisation category in Sri Lankan law comparable to most other countries in this dataset.
